pages.title: apex Overview
pages.description: What apex is: a modernised acme (three-button mouse, tags, columns, B2 execute, B3 look, plumbing) with a client–server split, embedded terminals for coding agents, remote attach over ssh, and a tool API that does not need 9P. Covers the main features, the three kinds of process (the apexd daemon, the gpui UI client, and tools and the CLI), and a map of the workspace crates, the Go SDK, providers, the mac bundle and the design documents (DESIGN.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, WEB.md, MODERN.md). Later pages cover the details; this one gives the big picture and where each part lives.

pages.title: Sessions, Shards and Leadership
pages.description: The model the whole system rests on: sessions, attachments and connections; state split into shards (buffer, window, layout, term, metalog, registry), each a replicated log; leasable versus pinned shards; leaders that sequence entries and followers that replay them; leases, fence epochs, transfer and reclaim (single-player mode). Explains why views live in the buffer shard and how ids are allocated without coordination. The entry types and apply are on the next page; the wire protocol is on attach-protocol.

pages.title: Entries, State and Apply
pages.description: apex-core's deterministic state machine: the entry and op types of each shard, `State::apply` as the only way state changes, the window, layout, term and meta structures (including Body kinds such as Text, Term and Page, settings, processes, notifications and the rule table), `State::hash` for divergence checks, and postcard snapshots. Also covers the core's test suite (scenario and property tests that compare follower replay and snapshot-plus-tail against the leader) and the benchmarks. Buffers and undo are on their own page.

pages.title: Buffers, Views and Undo
pages.description: How text is held and edited: rune-indexed text on a rope (`text.rs`) and its `apex_edit::Text` view; the buffer (acme's File) with version, dirty/stale flags and disk hash; views (selections and origins) adjusted by acme's textinsert/textdelete rules; Zerox; and undo/redo as entries whose inverses come from the history in the state, with undo groups. Also covers acme's B3 expansion (`expand.rs`) and the core's fuzzy matcher. How a leader turns typing into these entries is on the node page.

pages.title: The Node: Leading and Built-in Commands
pages.description: `Node`, the replica that the UI and the daemon both run: catching up as a follower, and as leader typing, selecting, cut/paste/undo, Look, lowering Edit programs into entries, and the built-in commands (New, Del, Zerox, Stash, Newcol, Delcol, Sort, Font, Get's dirty check, and so on). Covers exec entries and their handlers and statuses, the +Errors windows, notifications, navigation stacks, and the effect queues the node keeps for a client (warp, shows, gotos). Pixel layout is on the tiling page; the Edit language itself is on its own page.

pages.title: Tiling and Layout
pages.description: acme's tiling, ported from plan9port's cols.c, rows.c and wind.c: columns and windows as integer-pixel rectangles in the replicated Layout, tag wrapping, trimming to whole lines, grow, drag and minimize operations, and the stash of windows put away. Explains the `Info` trait that supplies font metrics (the client's, or `Headless`) and the deliberate choice to replicate pixel geometry, with the review's case for replicating logical layout instead. How the client animates and draws this is on the client pages.

pages.title: The Edit Language (apex-edit)
pages.description: apex-edit, a line-by-line port of acme's sam-style Edit command language and Plan 9 regular expressions: leftmost-longest regexps with forward and backward machines (regx.rs), the parser for addresses and commands (parse.rs), command semantics (exec.rs), and the change log that merges changes as acme does (elog.rs). Covers the `Edit::run` API, its changes, dot, output, warnings and intents, where acme and sam differ, and the golden and sam-differential tests. How the node lowers a run into entries is on the node page.

pages.title: The Server: Commands, Files and Processes
pages.description: apex-server's `Server`, everything with an effect on the world: running B2 commands and pipes through rc in the window's directory with $winid and $samfile, Kill and process groups, Get and Put, recognising the server's own writes, the file watcher on parent directories with base-versioned SetContent and Stale, the ⌘O finder walk, folder listings, cd and the session environment. The daemon process around it, the protocol and proposals have their own pages.

pages.title: The Daemon (apexd)
pages.description: `daemon.rs` and the `apexd` binary: one daemon per host holding many sessions, each with its authoritative Log, a Server and a follower replica; the single state-owning thread fed by connection readers and terminal events through a channel, with a writer thread per connection; the daemon leading a headless session as the SERVER attachment until a UI takes it over; registry, session creation and ending, profile and attach scripts, and the apex-bench measurements. The message formats are on attach-protocol.

pages.title: The Attach Protocol
pages.description: The wire between daemon and every client: postcard messages in u32 length-prefixed frames over a Unix socket or any byte stream, the `PROTOCOL` version and build id said first on every connection, and the ClientMsg/ServerMsg variants (Hello, Append, Entries, leases, Propose/Applied, Plumb/PlumbAck, Ask/Answer, Term*, Find*, Io). Covers the client side in `remote.rs`: `Link` driving a Node over a mirror Log that assigns sequence numbers ahead of the server, flush, and `Remote` for headless clients. Proposals have their own page.

pages.title: Proposals: How Others Change State
pages.description: How the server, tools and the CLI change shards they do not lead: the `Proposal` enum (opening windows and pages, ReplaceRange, Insert, SetContent, Exec, Goto, Navigate, flags such as Own, Live and Working, notifications, and so on), routing to the leader, `proposal::apply` lowering them into the leader's own entries, the Applied reply, and the version-conflict policies. Includes the review's critique and planned collapse into fewer proposals.

pages.title: Plumbing Rules and Verbs
pages.description: apex's plumber: the rule table in the metalog, rule predicates (text, file, kind, isfile, isdir, owner, window) and actions (edit, run, client, tool), priorities, template expansion of $0..$9, $file, $line and the rest, and the walk the server makes for B3 and for verbs offered in the tools menu, falling back to Look. Covers tool rules answered by PlumbAck with deadlines, rules that start their tool when first wanted (`start`), the session's default rules, and `apex plumb rule add`.

pages.title: Terminals
pages.description: Hosted terminals end to end: the pty and child process (pty.rs), libghostty-vt parsing the stream into a screen through the ghostty-vt-sys FFI crate and its C shim, the terminal loop turning the screen into TermOp rows on the daemon-led term shard, key encoding, OSC titles, OSC 7 directories, OSC 52 clipboard and progress, and window naming as DIR/-TITLE. Also covers how the client paints the grid (term_element.rs) with contrast correction. The win tool, a shell in a text window, is on its own page.

pages.title: Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501)
pages.description: How a program in a terminal says what it is doing: the OSC 7501 reports (state idle, working, done, blocked, error; kind, progress, app, title, msg), records keyed by id and replaced whole, clearing, and the limits and life rules in `status.rs`. Covers how the terminal loop reads reports, how records enter the replicated state and proposals, and how the agent tool, win and the client use them in place of their own status. The terminal plumbing itself is on terminals.

pages.title: The I/O Plane and Pages
pages.description: The Page window kind and the HTTP-shaped I/O plane multiplexed over the session socket: Body::Page with content from a buffer or a URL, fetched via the host, the client or a tool (tool:// and apextool://), the apexfile:// scheme, CONNECT and the proxy, file watches as streaming responses, page navigation, reload and scroll state in the log, and the script bridge (window.apex.send). Covers the client's WKWebView placement (web.rs, webbar.rs) and the page outline: headings shown as ticks in the page's scrollbar with a pointer-revealed list (outline.rs). The Web, Preview and diff tools that write pages are on the tools pages.

pages.title: Remote Hosts and Providers
pages.description: How apex attaches to sessions on other machines: session URLs (local:///, ssh://, sprite://), providers as `apex-remote-<provider> DESTINATION COMMAND` with ssh built in, installing the right apex and rc into ~/.apex/bin on the destination, `apex attach -stdio` bridging frames to the daemon's socket, and the build id that decides when to update. Covers the example provider scripts and the ssh test that fakes a host.

pages.title: The UI Client (apex-ui)
pages.description: The gpui client's architecture: `main.rs` and the command line, the `Acme` app in app.rs leading its shards through a Node, the Backend (a daemon over a socket, or Backend::Local in-process), sync and render, and painting text straight from core state (text_element.rs). Explains what the client handles itself rather than through the log and the review's notes on app.rs's size. Input, overlays, the window chrome and themes are on the child pages.

pages.title: Mouse, Keyboard and Look
pages.description: How the client turns input into editing: the three-button model and chords (opt-click B2, cmd-click B3), sweeps, B4 tools menu (menu.rs, after libdraw's menuhit), keyboard editing in text_key, the pointer warp after layout changes, caret and cursor drawing, ⌘F/⌘G and live Look as you type. Pickers and other overlays are on the next page.

pages.title: Pickers and Overlays
pages.description: The client's list pickers and overlay fields: ⌘P finder, ⌘O quickopen backed by the host's find job, the ⌘⇧P command palette, ^F inline completion, the tag head's path and label editing with its folder picker, the cwd picker, and the shared one-line field. Notes the matchers each uses and the review's proposal for one ListPicker and one overlay state.

pages.title: Sessions, Tabs and Window Chrome
pages.description: Everything around the tiled windows: tabs and the session pool (parked sessions), the session selector, the sidebar and title bar, the ctrl-tab switcher with session miniatures, the stash shelf and column strips, window glides, notifications and the Dock (attention.rs), toasts for diagnostic windows, the process pills, connection standing, and restarting a mismatched server. The underlying layout is on tiling-and-layout.

pages.title: Themes, Fonts and Colour
pages.description: The modern-mac look: the six palettes (Alabaster, Xcode, Classic, GitHub, Nova, rsms), each light and dark, derived from a few key colours; the bundled font sets and how they are chosen for text, mono, terminals and chrome; colour choices checked under a deuteranopia simulation; and terminal contrast correction in Oklab. Covers the assets directory and MODERN.md's rationale.

pages.title: The apex Command
pages.description: apex-cli, the stable public surface for scripts: Go-style flags, APEX_SOCKET and APEX_SESSION, and the subcommands (server, ls, stop, attach, new, open, win, text, edit, sel, exec, events, term, ps, kill, plumb, B, env, set, cat, io, tool, label, awd). Explains that each subcommand attaches as a tool with its own replica and proposes to the leader, so it works with no UI, plus apex-editor and xdg-open links. Profiles and settings are on the configuration page.

pages.title: Configuration: Profile, Attach and Settings
pages.description: How a user configures apex with no configuration file: the host's and the creator's ~/.apex/profile run when a session is made, ~/.apex/attach run on each attach, `apex env` for the session environment, `apex set` settings for the session or an attachment (Preview.EXT, lsp.LANG, lsp.root and others), the environment variables apex sets for commands, and the example profile for zsh, bash and fish.

pages.title: Writing Tools: the apex-tool SDK
pages.description: The extension point: apex-tool's `Tool` API for programs that join a session by name, make and write windows, offer verbs through rules, answer plumbs within their deadlines, watch other windows' edits, own windows, raise notifications and make pages. Covers next_event, insert_following, claiming built-in words such as Put, and the known gaps (filtered own edits, missing primitives). The JSON bridge and Go SDK, and the bundled tools, are on child pages.

pages.title: JSON Bridge and Go SDK
pages.description: Tools in other languages: `apex tool bridge NAME`, one JSON object per line on stdin and stdout with id-matched commands (windows, new, open, read, write, rule, ack, watch, page, diff, and the rest) and events (hello, plumb, edit, renamed, deleted, bye); and the Go package built on it, with Attach, Offer and Serve, plus the upper example. Notes where the surfaces disagree with the Rust SDK.

pages.title: win and Language Servers
pages.description: Two bundled tools: `apex tool win`, acme's win as a shell in an editable text window with output point, line-at-a-time sending, echo cancelling, Send and Snarfout; and `apex tool lsp`, one language server per workspace root, incremental document sync from the entry stream, UTF-16 position mapping, diagnostics in root/+lsp, and the Def Refs Type Hov Sig Fmt Rn verbs. Both use Remote and Proposal directly rather than the SDK.

pages.title: Preview, Web and Diff Tools
pages.description: The tools that write pages: `apex tool preview`, which pipes a buffer through the converter a Preview.EXT setting names (apex md for Markdown) into a page beside it and follows the caret; `apex tool web`, which answers Web and Newweb and keeps each page's history; and apex-diff, which lays out a unified diff side by side with links into the files. Covers rules that start these tools on first use and stop them when idle. The Page kind itself is on io-plane-and-pages.

pages.title: Coding Agents: apex tool agent and apex-acp
pages.description: How apex serves Claude Code, Codex and Muse running in its terminals: hooks installed into each agent's settings that append to ~/.apex/agent/SESSION.jsonl, the tool reading those logs, per-agent transcripts, preview pages and VCS diffs, permission answers (Allow, Deny, Ask), notifications, the overview pane, history, and the ls/wait/events commands. Also covers the experimental apex-acp, an Agent Client Protocol client living in an apex window.

pages.title: Building, Testing and Packaging
pages.description: How to build and test apex: the Cargo workspace and its profiles, the patched pathfinder_simd, the Zig-built libghostty-vt (APEX_GHOSTTY_SRC, APEX_GHOSTTY_LIB, ZIG), the build id hash, the CI workflow, and where each crate's tests and benchmarks live (including sam for the differential tests). Covers mac/build-app.sh making Apex.app with the apex command, rc, and a linux-amd64 build cross-linked with Zig for remote hosts, and the docs site.
